headline: WHO validates Timor-Leste's elimination of trachoma
meta_description: Timor-Leste becomes the last country in WHO's South-East Asia Region to eliminate trachoma, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness.
summary_short: Timor-Leste has been validated by WHO for eliminating trachoma as a public health problem, marking a major milestone for the entire South-East Asia Region.
body:
Trachoma, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness, has been eliminated as a public health problem across WHO's South-East Asia Region following Timor-Leste's validation.

Timor-Leste was the last remaining country in the region where trachoma was suspected to be endemic. With the nation's official elimination status, the entire South-East Asia Region is now free from trachoma as a significant health threat.

This milestone represents years of public health efforts and underscores the possibility of defeating preventable causes of blindness worldwide.
quick_facts: Trachoma is the world's leading infectious cause of blindness
Timor-Leste was the last endemic country in WHO's South-East Asia Region
Entire region now validated as trachoma-free
